screen1-a1.where: Top left corner, three short horizontal lines stacked, next to the big word 'messenger'.
screen1-a1.expectation: I think a side menu opens with more places to go in the app.
screen1-a1.cue: The three lines. I have seen that shape open a menu in other apps, but there are no words on it.

first_pass.why: I am fairly sure it is a menu, but I cannot tell what is in it until I open it, and a picture with no word means I have to remember the shape rather than read it. With speech, I would not know what to call it.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Menu' under the three lines.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "I am fairly sure it is a menu, but I cannot tell what is in it until I open it, and a picture with no word means I have to remember the shape rather than rea..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a1 (Top left corner, three short horizontal lines stacked, next to the big word 'messenger'.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I think a side menu opens with more places to go in the app."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I pressed the three lines on the chat list. A side menu slid out from the left: 'Ally Cooper' with a down arrow and a gear at the top, then Communities, Message requests, Archive, 'More' - Friend requests, 'Also from Meta' - Subscriptions, Facebook Reels, Facebook Events, Facebook Dating. The phone's Back closed it.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: It is a menu, as I thought, and everything inside it has words. I still had to guess from three lines to get there, but the guess was right and harmless.

screen1-a2.where: Top right, the first of two icons: a square with a pencil writing across it.
screen1-a2.expectation: I think it starts a new message to someone.
screen1-a2.cue: The pencil. A pencil means writing, and this is a messaging app, so writing probably means a new message.

first_pass.why: It could also mean 'edit' - edit my list, edit my profile. A pencil is used for both, and I would read it several ways before I committed.
first_pass.solution: A word under it such as 'New message'.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "It could also mean 'edit' - edit my list, edit my profile. A pencil is used for both, and I would read it several ways before I committed." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a2 (Top right, the first of two icons: a square with a pencil writing across it.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I think it starts a new message to someone."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I pressed the square with the pencil. A screen titled 'New message' opened, with 'To: Type a name or group', then 'New story', 'New note', 'Group chat' and a 'Suggested' list of people. The back arrow returned me to the chat list.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: It is 'new message', not 'edit'. The title of the screen settled my doubt the moment I got there, though nothing told me before I pressed.

screen1-a3.where: Top right corner, a dark circle with a letter 'f' in it.
screen1-a3.expectation: I think it takes me out of this app and into Facebook.
screen1-a3.cue: The letter f inside the circle. I can read the letter, not really recognise the logo as a picture.

first_pass.why: I am not certain it is Facebook, and I do not know whether it opens another app or a Facebook page inside this one. If it takes me out of this app I lose my place, and that is exactly what I fear.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Open Facebook' next to it, and make it clear it leaves Messenger.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "I am not certain it is Facebook, and I do not know whether it opens another app or a Facebook page inside this one. If it takes me out of this app I lose my ..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a3 (Top right corner, a dark circle with a letter 'f' in it.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I think it takes me out of this app and into Facebook."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I pressed the 'f' circle. Without any warning I was taken out of Messenger into the Facebook app, which first asked to send me notifications (I said Don't allow) and then showed Facebook's own Notifications page. I had to reopen Messenger myself to get back.

screen1-a3.closing_comment: It left the app entirely, with no warning and no way back by its own Back. That is exactly the loss of place I was afraid of, and worse than I expected.

screen1-a4.where: A blue strip right across the screen below the title, with the words 'Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on.'
screen1-a4.expectation: Notifications for this app get switched on.
screen1-a4.cue: The words themselves say it: 'Tap to turn on.'

first_pass.why: It tells me the situation and the action in one plain sentence. That is ideal for me.

screen1-a5.where: The long grey bar with a magnifying glass and the words 'Ask Meta AI or search'.
screen1-a5.expectation: I type in here, either to search for something or to ask an AI a question.
screen1-a5.cue: The magnifying glass and the words 'Ask Meta AI or search'.

first_pass.why: It says two things at once. I cannot tell whether what I type goes to a search of my chats and people, or to the AI, or which one wins. I would read that sentence over and over. And I do not know what 'Meta AI' is.
first_pass.solution: One job per box, or say plainly 'Search your chats and people' with an example, and put the AI somewhere separate.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "It says two things at once. I cannot tell whether what I type goes to a search of my chats and people, or to the AI, or which one wins. I would read that sen..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); tap the box tagged a5 (The long grey bar with a magnifying glass and the words 'Ask Meta AI or search'.), type something you would really put there, watch the screen while you type, then delete what you typed without sending anything
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: while you type you can no longer tell what the box is for, or it does not take what you expected (you said: "I type in here, either to search for something or to ask an AI a question.")
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen keeps showing what the box is for and it takes what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I tapped the bar and typed 'Krisna' - spelt wrongly on purpose, the way I often do. A results screen appeared with tabs 'All', 'People', 'Messages', 'Groups', 'Pages'; 'Krishna Bharti - Connected' came first, then 'More people'. A separate small 'Ask' button with the purple dots appeared at the right end of the box. I deleted my text; nothing was sent.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: Typing searches people and chats, it forgave my spelling and it sorted results into named tabs - all things that help me. The AI is a separate 'Ask' button. The words 'Ask Meta AI or search' still promise two things before I start, so it is not fully clear.

screen1-a6.expectation: Something to do with me - maybe adding my own story or writing a short note.
screen1-a6.cue: The word 'You' and the bubble 'Drop a thought'.

first_pass.why: There are three boxes on this one tile and I do not know which part does what. 'Drop a thought' is a figure of speech - drop it where, and who sees it?
first_pass.solution: Say what happens in plain words, for example 'Write a note your friends can see', and make the whole tile one thing.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "There are three boxes on this one tile and I do not know which part does what. 'Drop a thought' is a figure of speech - drop it where, and who sees it?" - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?

test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I pressed the 'You' tile (the grey person) and, separately, the speech bubble on it. Both opened the same 'New note' screen: 'Share a thought...' above my picture, and at the bottom 'Anyone can see your note on Messenger and Facebook for 24 hours.' I closed it with the X. I also noticed the bubble's words keep changing by themselves: 'Share a song', 'What's up?', 'Post a note...', 'Drop a thought'.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: The three boxes all do the same thing, and the note screen explains who sees it and for how long. But the tile itself never says 'note', and its words keep changing while I look at it.

first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Menu' under the three lines.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I think a side menu opens with more places to go in the app."), or you still cannot tell what it did

test_cases.what_happened: This box repeats on several screens; I ran it once and record the same outcome here. I pressed the three lines on the chat list. The phone's Back closed it.

screen25-a1.closing_comment: It is a menu, as I thought, and everything inside it has words. I still had to guess from three lines to get there, but the guess was right and harmless.

first_pass.solution: A word under it such as 'New message'.

first_pass.solution: One job per box, or say plainly 'Search your chats and people' with an example, and put the AI somewhere separate.
